answers.a: The Manila International Research Conference 2026 (MIRC 2026) is a hybrid international academic conference that brings together researchers, academicians, practitioners, policymakers and students from diverse disciplines. Its theme is “The role of Artificial Intelligence, sustainability and innovation in building resilient, inclusive and future‑ready communities,” and it will be held on 29–30 September 2026 at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) in Intramuros, Manila.

The Manila International Research Conference 2026 runs from 27 to 30 September 2026.  

- 27 September 2026: Hospitality & Tourism sub‑conference at De La Salle – College of Saint Benilde (DLSU‑CSB).  
- 29 – 30 September 2026 (Tuesday‑Wednesday): Main conference at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM).
The venue is Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM), located at Gen. Luna Cor. Muralla Streets, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines 1002.

answers.q: What is the address of the venue?
answers.a: The venue is at Gen. Luna Cor. Muralla Streets, Intramuros Manila, Philippines 1002.

answers.q: How do I get to PLM from the LRT?
answers.a: Take the Central Terminal (LRT‑1) station, which is the nearest LRT stop. From there it’s about an 860 m walk to the PLM campus—roughly an 11‑minute walk. Exit the station, head toward the walled‑city gates and follow the signs to the university entrance.
keys: How do I get to PLM from the LRT?

answers.q: What time does registration open on the first day?
answers.a: Registration opens at 7:00 AM on the first day (29 September 2026).

answers.a:
Registration is held in the **GEE Lobby** (the lobby of the Gusaling Emilio Ejercito Sr. building).  

- **Tuesday 29 September 2026:** 7:00 – 17:00  
- **Wednesday 30 September 2026:** 7:00 – 12:00  

These times and the venue are taken from the programme outline.

answers.q: How long do I get to present?
answers.a: Each presenter is allocated 12 minutes for the presentation, followed by a brief 3‑minute Q&A slot.

answers.q: How long is the question and answer portion?
answers.a: Each presentation is followed by a 3‑minute question‑and‑answer segment.

answers.a:
The conference has four tracks:

- BGL — Business, Government, Law  
- EASS — Education, Arts, Social Science, Social Work  
- HS — Health Sciences  
- STEA — Science, Technology, Engineering, Architecture
STEA stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, Architecture.
BGL stands for **Business, Government, Law**.
HS stands for Health Sciences.
EASS stands for **Education, Arts, Social Science, Social Work**.

answers.q: Which room is the STEA track in?
answers.a: The STEA track sessions are held in the Justo Albert Auditorium (code JAA) on the PLM campus.
keys: Which room is the STEA track in?

answers.q: Which room is the BGL track in?
answers.a: The BGL track sessions are held in **GEE KL – the GEE Katipunan Lounge** (room code KL) in the Emilio Ejercito Sr. Building.
keys: Which room is the BGL track in?

answers.q: Which room is the HS track in?
answers.a: The Health Sciences (HS) track sessions are held in the GK BTB room – the “GK Bukod Tanging Bulwagan” in the Gusaling Katipunan (GK) building.
keys: Which room is the HS track in?

answers.q: Which room is the EASS track in?
answers.a: The EASS track sessions are held in the **GA TOP** room (room code TOP) of the **Gusaling Don Pepe Atienza (Don Pepe Atienza Building)**. The full name of the TOP room has not been supplied in the congress material.
keys: Which room is the EASS track in?

answers.a: BTB is the room code for **GK Bukod Tanging Bulwagan** in the Gusaling Katipunan (GK) building.
KL is the abbreviation for the **Katipunan Lounge**, the room code “KL” in the GEE (Gusaling Emilio Ejercito Sr.) building.

answers.q: Where is the Justo Albert Auditorium?
answers.a: The Justo Albert Auditorium (building code JAA) is on the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) campus, at Gen. Luna Cor. Muralla Streets, Intramuros, Manila 1002, Philippines. It is one of the main lecture halls where the opening ceremony, plenary talks and many STEA sessions are held.
